# Tapua'i build layers

**Owner:** `ARCHITECTURE_SYNC` (reports to `ENGINEERING`). **Plan version:** `212176c4fb37`.
**Agents in registry:** 116. **Latest migration:** `20261114010000_user_feed_prefs.sql`.

Living map of how the app is built (L0–L9) and which callable roles sit on each layer.
When the owner prompts a stack/architecture change, `ARCHITECTURE_SYNC` updates this map,
announces it, and breaks the work into routed tasks so every named role updates its team
records, documents and owned code in the same turn. An announcement is a notice — not
proof that 116 specialists ran, a continuous worker is paid, or a release is approved.

**Status:** In use. Expo fan app, Expo /admin writes, Next read-only portal, Soft-Wall and role HQs.

**Pieces**

- Expo Router SDK 58 iOS / Android / web preview

## How updates work

1. Owner or lead prompts a change (`CALL: ARCHITECTURE_SYNC` with what moved).
2. `ARCHITECTURE_SYNC` edits `build-layers.json` (and any owned code/docs) in the same turn.
3. `pnpm layers:sync` regenerates this file; `pnpm layers:sync --acknowledge --by "<session>"`
   writes [ARCHITECTURE_CHANGE_LOG](../agents/ARCHITECTURE_CHANGE_LOG.md) with per-role tasks.
4. Each named role updates its team section, owned documents and code, then appends a review line.
5. `DOCUMENTATION` and `VP_OPERATIONS` reconcile shared docs and roster drift; `pnpm layers:check`
   (in `pnpm check` / CI) fails on a stale or unannounced map.

This is not a paid idle worker. Currency is enforced by the same-turn protocol + CI gate,
matching `EXIT_SYNC` / `INFRASTRUCTURE` — not by a background daemon.
